comparisons.peer_topic: Income tax provision increase due to IP transfer and supply chain realignment
comparisons.peer_summary: The provision for income taxes increased to $3,748 million in fiscal year 2024 from $1,015 million in 2023, primarily due to the impact of a non-recurring intra-group transfer of certain IP rights to the United States as a result of supply chain realignment.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and AVGO reported a significant increase in their income tax provision for fiscal year 2024 compared to 2023, but attributed the increases to different structural drivers. AMD's provision increased to $381 million primarily due to higher pre-tax income and a specific $373 million intercompany integration transaction. In contrast, AVGO's provision surged to $3,748 million from $1,015 million, driven by a non-recurring intra-group transfer of IP rights and a resulting shift in the jurisdictional mix of income, rather than just income growth.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation allowance and effective tax rate change
comparisons.peer_summary: The effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to the establishment of a valuation allowance against US federal deferred tax assets in 2024. This allowance was recognized in the third quarter of 2024 after determining it was more likely than not that the assets would not be recoverable, largely due to a three-year cumulative historical loss position resulting from asset impairment and restructuring charges.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and INTC disclosed changes in their effective tax rates in 2024 compared to 2023, but the drivers were opposing in nature regarding profitability and allowances. AMD's effective tax rate increased to 19% from a (68%) benefit rate, driven by higher pre-tax income and a large intercompany transaction. Conversely, INTC's effective tax rate increased because it established a valuation allowance against US federal deferred tax assets due to a three-year cumulative historical loss position, whereas AMD moved from a loss position (benefit) to a profit position (provision).

sentences.text: We recorded an income tax provision of $381 million in 2024 and an income tax benefit of $346 million in 2023, representing effective tax rates of 19% and (68%), respectively.
The increase in income tax provision in 2024 was primarily due to higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.

Our effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by the effects associated with the establishment of a valuation allowance against our US federal deferred tax assets in 2024.

As a result of our assessment in the third quarter of 2024, we determined it was more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable based upon our three-year cumulative historical loss position as of the third quarter of 2024, largely resulting from the asset impairment and restructuring and other charges incurred during the third quarter of 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fiscal Year 2024 Income Tax Expense and Rate
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA recognized income tax expense of $4.1 billion and an effective tax rate of 12.0% for fiscal year 2024, driven primarily by the FDII deduction, stock-based compensation, and U.S. federal research tax credits.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVDA recognized a positive income tax provision in fiscal year 2024, but their effective tax rates differed significantly from the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% due to distinct benefit drivers. AMD recorded an effective tax rate of 19%, slightly below the statutory rate, with the increase from 2023 driven by pre-tax income and an intercompany transaction. NVDA recorded an effective tax rate of 12.0%, also below the statutory rate, driven by benefits from the FDII deduction, stock-based compensation, and R&D tax credits.
